subject.title: Agent declared tools != effective session tools: no strict inheritance mode, no visibility, no clipping reason trace

question: Should OpenClaw add a strict tool-inheritance mode, or keep runtime clipping as the default and expose declared-vs-effective diagnostics plus structured blocked reasons?
rationale: The issue asks for new config/API/security behavior around tool enforcement; source shows current main only exposes effective tools and logs removals, so the next step depends on maintainer intent for default and fail-closed semantics.

options.title: Diagnostics-first contract
options.body: Expose declared/effective/removed tool diagnostics and blocked reasons without changing default enforcement semantics.

options.title: Strict inheritance mode
options.body: Add an explicit strict mode that fails sessions when effective tools diverge from declared policy, with migration/docs coverage.

options.title: Document current model
options.body: Leave runtime clipping and logs as-is and document that declared agent tools are not authoritative for a session.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics-first contract
recommendation.body: Expose declared/effective/removed tool diagnostics and blocked reasons without changing default enforcement semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history and ownership signals put the tool-policy/runtime contract closest to `steipete`, while adjacent implementers can help with the API details.
